subject: using bcsft and riself to construct a genetic map of RILs

messages.author: a88e586574ebf833
messages.subject: using bcsft and riself to construct a genetic map of RILs
parts:
Dear all,

I was working on the 4K GBS markers to construct genetic map of a F7 population. These 4k markers were the most confident markers in our data and they were ordered by physical position.


After removing the suspect and redundant markers, the 1K remaining markers were used to construct genetic map and I found the total map distance were quite different when I treated data as “bcsft” (F.gen=7) and “riself”.


The total map distance is about 960cM and 1820cM when I treated data as “bcsft” (F.gen=7) and “riself”, respectively. And I also found if I treat data as “f2”, I will get 1820cM just like treat it as ”riself”.


Here is my code and genetic map:


rils1=read.cross(file = "markers (delete suspect).csv" ,error.prob = 0.001,  genotypes = c("A","H","B"), alleles = c("A","B"), estimate.map = T , F.gen = 7, map.function = "kosambi")

rils2=read.cross(file = "markers (delete suspect).csv" ,error.prob = 0.001,  genotypes = c("A","H","B"), alleles = c("A","B"), estimate.map = T , crosstype = "riself", map.function = "kosambi")

rils3=read.cross(file = "markers (delete suspect).csv" ,error.prob = 0.001,  genotypes = c("A","H","B"), alleles = c("A","B"), estimate.map = T , crosstype = "f2", map.function = "kosambi")

 

 

As I know, the map distance will inflate in RILs because of more generation allowed for recombination.

Is the expansion in RILs considered only if I treat data as “bcsft”?

 

Thank you

messages.author: 6f0e81f2684a02bb
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] using bcsft and riself to construct a genetic map of RILs
parts:
Genetic map distances can shrink or expand if the expected genotype frequencies deviate from Mendelian expectations of the cross type. Although, it does seem strange that your F2 map and RIL map look practically identical. Would you please share the output of summary statistics of your cross objects (e.g. >summary(rils1); >summary(rils2); >summary(rils3) ) so that we can see what type of genotype frequencies/distribution you are working with?

Thanks,
Sandra Truong
